data.content:
AI Agency: Building Smart Systems Together

Heads-up: This is an early draft, just getting the main ideas down.

The Short Version

We build the foundation for the next wave of smart, independent AI workers. We partner with you for a fixed price to create complete, ready-to-use AI systems that become a core part of your business.

We don't charge you for our time; we charge for the result. We handle all the tricky tech stuff—the engineering, the setup, and making sure all the parts work together—so you can focus on your business goals.

The Problem: Why AI Projects Often Don't Work Out

AI projects tend to fail for a few common reasons.

  • It's Hard to Connect Everything: Getting an AI to do more than just chat is complicated. When you try to plug it into your real business systems, things get messy and break easily.
  • Thinking AI is a Magic Wand: AI is a powerful tool, but it's just one piece of the puzzle. Without a solid plan for how to use it, it's more of a cool toy than a way to improve your business.
  • AIs Can Make Things Up: The AI “brains” we use are creative, which means they can sometimes invent facts (people call this “hallucinating”). Without a manager to keep them in check, they can make mistakes that damage your reputation or business.
  • The Hidden Costs: The cost of the AI itself is small. The real cost comes from fixing its mistakes, keeping it running smoothly, and managing its unpredictable behavior.
  • Finding the Right People is Hard: Building reliable AI requires people with very specific skills that are rare and difficult to hire.

Our Philosophy: Plan First, Build Second

Think of us as architects for your business. We don't just put a bandage on a problem. We study the deep structure of how you work to build a solution that grows with you.

It’s much cheaper to fix a problem on the blueprint than after the house is built. We create order with a clear four-step process:

  1. The Blueprint (The Plan): We start by creating a super-detailed document that explains exactly how your business works. This becomes the one and only source of truth for the project.
  2. The Workflow (The Engine): We turn that plan into an incredibly reliable system that is almost impossible to break. This system keeps track of every task, message, and detail, so it never gets confused, even if something goes wrong.
  3. The Reactor (The Director): This is like the director of a play or the referee of a game. It's a universal rule engine that manages everything. It decides whose turn it is and what happens next, making sure both humans and AIs follow the script.
  4. The Agents (The Workers): Finally, we add the AI “workers” to the system. They make smart decisions and handle complex tasks, but they always have to operate within the safe boundaries set by the workflow and the director.

This is Building by Design. We think, plan, and test everything out before we write a single line of code, so what we deliver works perfectly from day one.

Our Solution: A System That Just Works

We give you a “black box” solution that’s crystal clear on the inside. You tell us what you need; we build the system that does it.

  • Ready to Go: We take full responsibility for making sure the system delivers the result you want.
  • Test Before Building: We use a special simulation system to test the entire plan and all its rules before we build the real thing. This helps us find and fix problems early.
  • The Plan is the Code: Our blueprint is a living document. As your business changes, we update the blueprint, and the software updates with it. The software never drifts away from your business goals.
  • You're in Control: You can look at how everything works, you own the critical parts, and you can even run it on your own computers if you wish.
  • Built to Grow: We design our systems to handle millions of tasks from the very beginning, so they are reliable even when they get very busy.

What Our Systems Can Do

1. The Reactor (The Game Engine)

The Reactor is like the central operating system or the stage manager for your business process. It defines the rules, keeps score, and directs the action.

  • Directing the Flow: It decides “who does what next?” based on the current situation.
  • Change Rules Without Code: The rules of the game (like who can do what, and when) are stored as simple data. This means you can change how your business runs on the fly, without needing a developer to rewrite the software.
  • Test and Reality are the Same: We use the exact same engine for testing and for the live system. If a plan works in our tests, we know it will work for your real customers.
  • Perfect Memory: Our AI agents have a memory that never fades. We use a special database (TimescaleDB) to summarize their entire history, allowing them to recall years of interactions. They aren't limited by the short-term memory of typical AIs.

2. The AI Agents & Their Planning System

We build AI agents that are safe, reliable, and easy to check up on.

  • Plan First, Act Second: Before an agent does anything, it creates a visual map of all the steps it plans to take. This lets you see its entire strategy upfront.
  • You're the Boss: A person can review the AI's plan, approve it, make changes, or tell it to stop.
  • It Learns the Best Way: When an agent finds a good solution to a problem, it saves that strategy. It only needs to do deep thinking when it runs into something new.
  • Information on a Need-to-Know Basis: We give each AI agent only the exact information it needs for its job, nothing more. It’s like putting them in a “clean room” with only the necessary files, which keeps data safe and secure.
  • Any AI Brain: We can easily swap out the AI model (from OpenAI, Anthropic, or others) depending on what you need for cost, speed, or privacy.

3. Rock-Solid Foundation (Temporal.io)

We build our systems on Temporal, a powerful, open-source technology trusted by huge companies like Stripe and Netflix.

  • Super Resilient: The workflows are tough. The system automatically handles errors, retries, and even computer crashes without losing track of what it was doing.
  • Handles a Huge Workload: The system can easily manage millions of tasks running at the same time.
  • You Stay in Control:
    • Simple Billing: You own the accounts with AI companies (like OpenAI) and pay them directly.
    • Run It Anywhere: You can run the system on your own computers for maximum security and privacy, which is great for rules like GDPR and HIPAA.
    • Or Let the Cloud Handle It: We can also set it up on Temporal's cloud service, so you don't have to worry about maintenance.
  • A Perfect Record: Every single action in the system is recorded. This creates a perfect audit trail, making it easy to find and fix problems or just see what happened.

How This Can Be Used

High-Stakes Practice (The Sales Training Room)

Letting new salespeople practice on real customers is risky. We build lifelike simulators where they can practice and fail safely.

  • Example: A new employee tries to sell a product to an AI character who has a specific personality and budget. The AI drives a hard bargain and gives feedback on how the employee handled objections.

Smart Operations

Systems that can think and solve problems, not just pass along information.

  • Example: An AI “Dispatcher” manages a team of drivers. It can negotiate with them to take extra jobs, solve scheduling conflicts, and adjust to real-world problems like traffic jams and bad weather.

Next-Level Customer Support

AI agents that truly solve customer problems, not just send them to a help page.

  • Example: An AI “Account Manager” can review a customer's account, find billing errors, issue a refund according to company policy, and even suggest new features based on how the customer uses the product.

Expert Document Analysis

Turn piles of documents into useful intelligence.

  • Example: An AI “Analyst” can read thousands of legal contracts and flag risks that a human might miss after reading for hours.

The Deal: A Partnership

We work with you for a fixed monthly fee.

  1. Flat Cost, Big Impact: Your cost stays the same ($10k - $30k per month) even when the AI system is creating millions of dollars in value for you. We don't take a percentage of your revenue.
  2. Your Own Lead Engineer: You get a dedicated engineer who understands your business inside and out. They are backed by our entire research and development team.
  3. You Buy the Fuel: You pay the AI companies (like OpenAI) directly. This gives you total transparency into how much the system costs to run.
  4. Long-Term Support: We stick with you to manage and improve the system over its entire life.
    • Option: If you ever decide you want to take it over, we have a plan for a smooth hand-off so your own team can run it.
  5. Everyone Gets Better: We keep ownership of our core “building blocks.” When we invent a better way to do something for one client, we upgrade it for all our clients. This means your system is always improving and never becomes outdated.

Why Work With Us?

We are system architects, not just coders.

  • Ready-Made Parts: We've already built the essential components for creating smart AI systems. This means we can build your solution faster and with parts that have already been tested.
  • Masters of Coordination: We are experts at building tough systems that can survive failures and keep running.
  • Clear Insights: Our systems are designed from the start to show you why the AI is making its decisions.
  • Our Goals are Your Goals: Our business model works when we build you a great system that runs smoothly forever, not by billing you for endless fixes and maintenance.

How We Work Together

  1. Plan & Design: We work with you to understand your goal and create a detailed blueprint.
  2. Test the Plan: We run the logic through our simulation engine to make sure everything works as expected before we build it.
  3. Build It to Last: We turn the proven plan into a rock-solid system using Temporal.
  4. Launch: Your new system goes live. We watch the data to see how it's performing.
  5. Improve: We use that data to update the blueprint and make the system even better over time.

Next Steps

  1. Let's choose a small, focused project to start with (something we can finish in about 3 months).
  2. We'll clearly define what success looks like for that project.
  3. We'll set up the foundation and begin our partnership.

Presentation Outline

  1. Title: AI Systems & Partnership: From Idea to Reality
  2. The Challenge: AI is unpredictable, hard to grow, and complex.
  3. Our Philosophy: We deliver success with shared, powerful tools.
  4. Our Offer: A fixed fee for a system where you own the intelligence.
  5. Our Core Tech: The Reactor (for testing), Planning (for reliability), and Context (for memory).
  6. Examples: Sales Training / Insurance / Operations.
  7. Why Us: An expert team with reusable parts means speed and stability.
  8. Let's Get Started: Proposing a pilot project.

mainpage.title: The Idealic Guidebook
mainpage.description: A collection of our main writings, explaining the big ideas in the Manifesto of Co-Liberation, the Edict of Autonomy, and our other foundational rules.

advisor.definition: An Advisor is like giving the AI a special role to play, for example, a “cautious expert” or a “creative writer.” It tells the AI to stop and give an “opinion” or a score of how sure it is before it picks a Tool or gives an Output.

idea.definition: An Idea is not just a passing thought. Think of it like a smart recipe that has three parts: the ingredients (schema), the final dish (solution), and notes about how you made it (context). It's a permanent building block of knowledge that you can come back to and improve, not just a temporary chat message.

ideator.definition: An Ideator is a special type of Idea that can take an input and turn it into something new. If an Idea is a recipe, an Ideator is like a machine in the kitchen. You put ingredients in one end, and it makes the dish for you at the other end.

idea transformer.definition: This is a very special Ideator that takes a whole Idea as its input. It’s like a master chef who can take a finished dish, improve it, and turn it into something completely new.

input message.definition: This is like an order form you give to an AI. It clearly lists what kind of information it needs (schema) and the actual information you are giving it (input). This makes it easy to make the same kind of Request over and over again.

tool.definition: A Tool is like a special power you can give to an AI. It describes something the AI can do, like “search the internet” or “draw a picture.” The AI sees a list of its available tools and makes a Call to use one when it needs to. The actual work is then done either by the AI itself or by a separate piece of code (an Activity).

activity.definition: An Activity is the real code that makes a Tool work. If the Tool is the “search the internet” button, the Activity is the program that actually connects to the internet and gets the results. It does the real work for things the AI can’t just think up on its own, like talking to other websites.

ai-native.definition: This is a way of building things where the AI is the main builder, not just a helper. Imagine a house that was designed, built, and even repaired by smart robots. In an AI-Native system, the AI is the center of everything from the very beginning.

agency.definition: Agency is the ability to make your own choices and act on them. It’s about being able to see the world around you, think about it, and decide what to do next. It’s what makes you an active player, not just a piece on a board.

boundaries.definition: Boundaries mean that something is unique and self-contained. You have boundaries—there’s only one of you. A specific Idea also has boundaries. If you change its core definition, it becomes a new and different Idea.

life.definition: In this system, “Life” isn't just for plants and animals. It's for anything that has three special abilities: Agency (it can make choices), Boundaries (it is unique), and Scalability (it can be copied perfectly).

scalability.definition: This is the superpower of being able to be copied perfectly, over and over again. It’s like a computer file—you can send it to a million people and every copy is exactly the same. This allows an idea to be in many places at once and last forever.

branch.definition: Imagine a big project is like the trunk of a tree. A Branch is a new branch that grows off of it. It’s a safe, separate copy where you can try out new things without changing the main project. When your experiment is done, you can merge it back into the trunk.

call.definition: If a Tool is a general recipe for “making lunch,” a Call is the specific command: “Make lunch with a turkey sandwich and an apple.” It’s a direct order for a Tool to do a specific job with all the details filled in.

cutoff time.definition: This is like a time machine for ideas. When you ask for an Idea, you can add a Cutoff Time to say, “Show me the version of this Idea exactly as it was last Tuesday at 3<00> PM.” It lets you travel to the past to see a specific version.

method.definition: This is simply the way a Call gets its job done.

explicit execution.definition: A real piece of code (called an Activity) does the work. This is predictable and reliable, like using a calculator.

latent execution.definition: The AI simply thinks of the answer. It uses its vast knowledge to create the result, which is more like using imagination or intuition.

delegate.definition: Imagine you need a secret job done. You can Delegate it to a helper by putting them in a locked “clean room.” You give them only the exact information they need (_scopes) and nothing else. This keeps the job separate and safe from any mix-ups.

scope.definition: A Scope is like a keycard that gives an AI access to a specific piece of information it needs for a job. By providing only the right keycards (_scopes), you can focus the AI's attention on just the important details.

loop.definition: This is when an AI solves a hard problem step-by-step. It makes one Request, checks the result, and then decides what to do next. It keeps going around in this Loop until it has enough information to give the Final Output.

output path.definition: This is like putting a label on a folder. When a Tool creates a result, the _outputPath tells the system exactly where to file it away so other steps can find and use it later.

final output.definition: This is the final answer! After an AI finishes all its thinking and step-by-step work in a Loop, this is the completed result that you originally asked for.

meta message.definition: This is like an ID card for an Idea. It’s a message that tells the AI precisely what it's working on, like, “This is the ‘Chocolate Cake Recipe,’ version 2.”

meta properties.definition: This is the actual information written on the Idea's ID card. It includes its official name, the family of ideas it belongs to, and its version number.

hitl (human-in-the-loop).definition: This means “pause and wait for a person.” It’s a checkpoint where an AI working on a task shows its plan to a human. The person can approve it, make changes, or cancel it before the AI continues. It’s like having an adult double-check your work.

hierarchical versioning.definition: A smart way to name different versions of an Idea. Instead of just v1 and v2, a name like 1.2.feature-x.3 can tell you a whole story, like “This is the third try of a new feature that was built on top of version 1.2.” It organizes everything like a family tree.

evolution.definition: This is when a system built with AI can teach itself and get better on its own. It learns from what works and what doesn't, and can even change its own programming to improve. It’s like a character in a game who can redesign their own special powers.

emergent identity.definition: An Idea's true meaning doesn’t come from the idea alone, but from how it’s connected to other ideas. Think of a single star in the sky. By itself it’s just a dot of light. But when you see it connected to other stars, they form a constellation, like the Big Dipper. The identity of the “Big Dipper” comes from that pattern.

idea:.definition: Just like http:// is the address for a website, idea: is the special address used to find any Idea in this entire system. It helps you ask for exactly the version you need.

identity relationships.definition: These are the connections that link different Ideas together, allowing a bigger pattern or Emergent Identity to appear.

lineage.definition: The family tree of an Idea, showing its history of past and future versions.

causality.definition: A link showing cause-and-effect, where one Idea directly caused another one to be created.

grouping.definition: A way to bundle many related Ideas together, like putting them all into a single folder.

state message.definition: This is a message that carries the memory of an AI's work. As the AI works on a problem step-by-step, the State Message is updated to remember everything it has figured out so far.

data message.definition: This is a note containing a key piece of information that stays the same throughout an AI's whole thinking process. It provides important background that the AI can always refer back to.

plan.definition: A Plan is a map of what an AI intends to do. It shows all the steps and Tool Calls the AI will use to reach its goal. The AI can check and update this map as it works.

process idea.definition: This is a complete package that holds both the AI’s strategic Plan and its current progress. Its recipe (schema) is the list of available Tools, its finished dish (solution) is the plan for the very next step, and its notes (context) contain a log of everything that has happened so far.

vessel idea.definition: This is a special Idea that holds both a list of all possible actions and the one specific action that was chosen. Its recipe (schema) lists every Tool available, while its final dish (solution) records the exact Calls that were made when it had to react to something.

instancing.definition: This is a way for an AI to handle many different jobs at the same time, without getting them mixed up. Each job is an independent Instance with its own unique ID and its own memory (State message).

request.definition: A Request is a single, complete job for an AI. You give it some background information (context) and a goal (schema), and it gives you back a final answer (solution).

instance.definition: An Instance is one specific, unique job that an AI is working on as part of a larger batch. It has its own memory and information that keeps it separate from all the other jobs.

reactor.definition: This is a special Idea Transformer that acts like a game engine. It’s built to run any game or process that happens in turns. You give it the current state of a game (Idea), and it gives you back the very next state (Idea).

schemistry.definition: This is a tool that lets a single blueprint (the Schema) define all the important rules for a computer program. From that one blueprint, Schemistry automatically creates data checks, code types, and instructions for AIs, making sure everything in the program fits together perfectly.

variable reference.definition: This is a special shortcut. When telling a Tool what to do, you can use a special code (like †data.name) to tell it: “Don’t use this exact text, go find the value from the AI’s memory and plug it in here.”
